confirmed.problem: Planning opens as a 388px overlay, not as reserved layout. confirmed.consequence: Orla opens Planning from the head to give five undated tasks a day, and a fifth of her board — everything finished — silently ceases to exist, along with the count on Waiting and half its sentence. confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED, and the cause is worse than the seat knew: the fix for this is already written in the source and is dead code.

Driven in Chromium at `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, clicking `[data-act="planning"]`:

- 1440: `.sheet` computed `margin-right: 0px`; sheet 100–1422, drawer 1034–1422, board `scrollWidth === clientWidth === 1322`, maxScroll 0. Trays: todo 116–374, doing 374–632, review 632–890, waiting 890–1148, done 1148–1406. DONE is 258 of 258px covered, WAITING loses 114px. The screenshot confirms it visually: WAITING's description is guillotined mid-word at "a deliver", its count is gone, and DONE is not on screen at all.
- 1920: same shape — board 1802/1802, maxScroll 0, done 1532–1886 inside a drawer at 1514–1902.
- Live region: only "Planning open." `.tray[data-lane="done"]` has `inert === false`, no `aria-hidden`, 20 tabbables. ArrowRight from the first card: doing → review → **done card at x=1161, behind the opaque panel**, and it stops there; Enter announces "Showing the whole note." with nothing visible changing.
- Share (x 1180), Planning (1260) and More (1357) are all under the panel with `tabIndex 0`.
- Spine round trip Tasks→Notes→Tasks: drawer still open, announcement "Tasks. 5 of 13 done.", board still 1322/1322.

ROOT CAUSE, which raises this above the seat's own framing. `src/tasks.css:1071/1079/1086` (and the breakpoint overrides at 1683/1718) already do exactly what the seat asks:

    [data-app="tasks"] .floor:has(.drawer) .sheet { margin-right: calc(388px + var(--inset)); }
    [data-app="tasks"] .floor:has(.drawer) .board { grid-auto-flow: column; grid-auto-columns: minmax(258px,1fr); scroll-snap-type: x proximity; }

with a comment that names this exact failure as already fixed: "Before this the drawer was white on white with no edge: it sliced the Waiting column mid-word and erased Done entirely, which read as the board breaking rather than a panel opening."

The selector matches nothing. The DOM is `.floor#deck > div[data-app="tasks"] > (.sheet, .drawer)` — `.floor` is the **ancestor** of `[data-app="tasks"]`, not a descendant. Measured: `document.querySelectorAll('[data-app="tasks"] .floor').length === 0`, while `.floor:has(.drawer).length === 1`. All five rules are inert. This is precisely the class of defect this engagement exists to find: a fix that held when Tasks was a standalone sheet and died when the three products were mounted under one floor.

Not a gate restatement — `interaction-check.mjs` has zero assertions containing "planning" or "drawer". Not on the closed list. Not taste.

Blocking, not defect: a whole lane is 100% occluded with maxScroll 0 so no scroll can recover it, and the keyboard rover walks focus onto an element behind an opaque surface and announces a state change the operator cannot see. Escape does close the drawer, so the operator is not trapped — but "the product will not do what it says" is met twice over.

The proposed fix is refuted only on its numbers, not its direction, so I am confirming and correcting in sharpenedFix: the breakpoints are 1200 and 900 in this source, not the 1024 and 768 the seat cites, and narrowing `.board` rather than `.sheet` forces a second edit for the head controls that the shipping intent gets for free.

confirmed.sharpenedFix:
One writer, one call site, and a rail guard.

1. Lift 943–961 into `function writeGap(measureEl)` and call it ONCE at the top of `place()`, immediately after the `if (!measureEl) return;` and BEFORE the `placeAcross` dispatch at 841. Then delete the block from the down branch entirely — do not also call it from the tail of `placeAcross()`, as the finding proposes. Two call sites re-open the "ONE WRITER" invariant the 950–954 comment was written to protect, and buy nothing: the sentence depends on `data-away`/`data-date`, not on where placement puts the pixels, so it is correct before either instrument runs.

2. Inside `writeGap`, take the live rows, `Number(el.getAttribute("data-away"))`, keep `> 0`, take the minimum, and read that row's `data-date`; fall back to `"Nothing is planned yet."` when the filtered set is empty. Keep `field.__gapAtRest = atRest` and the `__gapSpeak()` / `textContent` tail exactly as they are — the scrolled reading in `across` (static `.b-stick`) then paints the fresh at-rest string through the same door.

3. Guard the back rail: `if (measureEl.getAttribute("data-back") === "true") return;` as the first line of `writeGap`. `backMeasure()` (1103–1127) builds `.b-measure.b-back` with negative `data-away`, and `behindBlock({owner:true})` renders it inside the SAME `.b-field` as the horizon (2248). `settle` places every measure in the document (2955). Without the guard, a plan with a past would place the back rail second, find no positive `away`, and clobber a true sentence with "Nothing is planned yet." The current fixture has no past moments at the clock — I confirmed one `.b-measure` and zero `.b-back` in owner-flight, desk and phone — so this is latent today and lethal the day the fixture grows one.

confirmed.element: src/app.js `writeUrl()` (line ~296) and its catch; src/tasks.js:1478 `const history = [];`
confirmed.problem: `writeUrl()` throws on every platform, and its catch blames the wrong cause. tasks.js:1478 declares `const history = []` at classic-script top level, so in the composed document that binding lives in the global lexical environment and shadows `window.history` for every script in the realm — app.js's IIFE included. Measured in the page's own global scope on `_gate-suite.html`: `Array.isArray(history) === true`, `typeof history.replaceState === "undefined"`, `history === window.history` is `false`, `typeof window.history.replaceState === "function"`, and `history.replaceState(null,'','?x=1')` throws "history.replaceState is not a function". Confirmed behaviourally over http://localhost as well as file://: switching Tasks → Notes → Timeline leaves `location.search` at its opening value, and reloading that href reopens Tasks. The comment above it says "a sandboxed artifact frame and a file:// URL both refuse replaceState" and the catch says "Deep links still arrive; this one just cannot be written back" — both describe a conditional failure that is in fact unconditional, which is why nobody caught it. A second defect hides behind the first: `writeUrl()` copies `query.get("state")` forward unchanged, and `query` still holds the DEPARTING product's state after the compound split, so once the shadow is lifted a switch from `?state=tasks.board` to Notes writes `?p=notes&state=board` — a link that does not reproduce the surface it was written from.
confirmed.consequence: The router's stated contract — "The URL is a deep link and a gate handle" — is inoperative. Orla switches to Notes, her browser restores the tab or she reloads, and she is back on Tasks; a link she copies to send herself always points at whichever product the page opened on. Every gate and shot handle keeps working only because they set the URL rather than read it back, which is exactly the condition under which a silently swallowed exception survives 216 assertions.
confirmed.fix: Rename tasks.js's module-scope array (`const undoHistory = []`, updating its ~10 references at :779, :1478, :1492–1493, :1549–1551, :1586, :1593, :2673) so nothing shadows `window.history`, and address `window.history.replaceState` explicitly in `writeUrl()` rather than the bare identifier. The file's own doctrine agrees with the seat — src/app.js:311 says "A crossing is one act with two halves, so it has one undo." Tasks denying that undo exists, inside a suite that insists it is one application, is an untrue claim: misleading, not defect.

BUT BOTH HALVES OF THE FIX MAKE THE WORK WORSE, so the finding as filed is refuted.

(1) "call the seam's `uncross` for it" produces a HALF-UNDONE seam. `uncross` (src/app.js:343) only does `api.remove(id)` and `delete crossings[noteId]`. The Notes half — `Object.assign(note, before)`, `CROSSED.shift()`, `sentTask = null`, `decided.pop()` — lives in the closure passed to `offerUndo` (src/notes.js:1092 and :1135) and is unreachable from Tasks. "if `window.__SUITE` holds a live crossing for a card currently on the board" stays true for the whole session. So: cross, move a card, Ctrl+Z (undoes the move), Ctrl+Z again — and under this fix the second press silently deletes a card that crossed twenty minutes ago, announcing a seam sentence about an act nobody just performed. An undo that reaches past its own stack boundary and eats an old object is the worst class of failure in this file, and the fix has no ordering rule for multiple crossings either.

(3) The fallback string is a fresh lie. `?state=tasks.board`, no crossing anywhere, Ctrl+Z → "Nothing left to undo." That is the same code path. Replacing it with "Undo for that crossing is in Notes" tells a person on a cold board about a crossing that does not exist.

REFUTED ON THE FIX, NOT THE PROBLEM. The observation reproduces verbatim — do not discard it — but the proposed fix would ship a false instruction, and its stated alternative is unimplementable as written and more destructive than the finding claims.

DRIVEN (chromium, 1440x960, ?v=paper&state=tasks.board), in order: focus demo-t-01 -> Space -> "Picked up Confirm marquee sides with the hire company." -> ArrowRight -> "In progress, position 1 of 4." -> click .rail [data-rail="notes"] -> "Notes. 14 notes.", activeElement MAIN.sheet, card still aria-grabbed="true" data-force="moving" -> click [data-rail="tasks"] -> say = "Tasks. 5 of 13 done.", activeElement MAIN.sheet, held card force=moving, transform matrix(1.02,...), box-shadow rgb(79,70,229) 0 0 0 1.5px. Re-focus, ArrowRight -> "Review, position 1 of 3." Escape -> "Move cancelled. Confirm marquee sides with the hire company is back in the to do column." Every number and every sentence in the finding is exact. The cause is structural: the pointerdown handler that already ends a carry lives on window.__SUITE.host("tasks") (src/tasks.js:2711), and the spine sits outside it, so the one law tasks.js states in its own comment at endCarry — "The hand ends where the operator's attention goes" — is enforced for four vectors (pointer off the card, the composer, the Planning drawer, the tick) and not for the fifth.

WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED.

1. It names the wrong key. The proposed sentence says "Enter to drop it here". Enter does not drop. Driven: Space, then Enter -> "Showing the whole note.", carry still live (aria-grabbed still true). Space drops (tasks.js:1881-1899); the foot pill footPill() already prints the true vocabulary, "arrows move / Space drop / Esc cancel". Shipping this sentence puts an instruction into the spoken channel that does nothing — the exact failure endCarry's own comment names ("a foot pill printing instructions that no longer worked").

2. It throws away the arrival line. The replacement announcement never says "Tasks", so a person who just pressed a spine tile is no longer told which product they landed on. go() composes LABEL + summary for a reason.

3. The alternative half cannot be built as specified. "Dropping the carry at the point the spine is used ... must announce the drop" — but say() writes textContent on one shared #say region (app.js:181-196), and go() calls say(LABEL + ". " + summary) synchronously in the same tick. A drop sentence emitted before that is overwritten and never read. As stated, the alternative announces nothing.

4. The two options are not "equally acceptable" — the drop is the worse one. A completed keyboard carry records no undo entry: driven, Space -> ArrowRight -> Space gives "Confirm marquee sides ... dropped in the in progress column.", then Ctrl+Z gives "Nothing left to undo." So force-dropping at the spine converts a live, Escape-reversible carry into an irreversible move. The finding's own harm ("undoing a move the person watched land") is real, but its preferred remedy strands the opposite harm.

5. One material omission in the framing. "Returning armed, unfocused and silent" is true only of the spoken channel. Measured on return: the foot pill is still rendered at top=826 reading "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company | arrows move | Space drop | Esc cancel", and the held card is in view at 195..334 with its ring. The board's declared "only statement of what it is currently doing" is present and correct, so a sighted keyboard user is not left guessing. The real, unguarded case is narrower than stated: the arrival announcement omits the modal state, and focus lands on the sheet instead of the thing in hand.

SEVERITY. Defect, not blocking or misleading. No advertised affordance fails — the arrows move the card because a carry genuinely is live, and aria-grabbed="true" is exposed on the card for anyone who navigates to it. Nothing untrue is asserted. What is wrong is that the suite's most stateful moment survives a product switch without a word.

Nothing in interaction-check.mjs asserts j, k, or keep (I grepped), so the regression would ship with all 216 assertions green.

The seat's implied class is right at defect, not higher: the body advertises "with the arrow keys" and the arrows all work; the pick and its bar survive the tear intact, so nothing is lost and nothing untrue is asserted. It is a real hole — the file already names and fixed this exact class one plane over (3705-3711: "the hand owns these keys while it is up; if focus has drifted, they bring it back to the card rather than moving anything") and the notebook body is the unpatched instance — but it is passable, not blocking.
